If sentiment is negative in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 1.5–2.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to align with downward momentum.

If sentiment is positive and forecast peaks > +3% above recent high, reduce forecast by 2–4% for mid horizon (8–15 days) to prevent over-optimism.

If sentiment is mixed or neutral and forecast shows sustained upward trend, reduce forecast by 1–3% for late horizon (16–30 days) to account for mean reversion.

If sentiment is negative and forecast is below recent low, increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon to avoid underestimating rebound potential.

If sentiment is positive and forecast is below recent low, increase forecast by 1–2% for mid horizon to capture sentiment-driven reversal.

If sentiment is negative and forecast is above recent high, reduce forecast by 2–4% for late horizon to avoid overcorrection from sentiment-driven overbought conditions.
